title: Wings live: Madison Square Garden, New York City | 1976
content:
Wings performed at Madison Square Garden in New York City, NY, USA, on 25 May 1976.

It was the 43rd night of the 65-date Wings Over The World Tour, which ran from September 1975 to October 1976, and the second of two consecutive nights in New York City.

The proceeds of this show were donated to Phoenix House, a drug treatment centre that had supported Paul McCartney when he was trying to obtain a US visa following his drug convictions in Sweden and Scotland. At the time he had offered to play a benefit show for them, and this was his way of making good on the promise.

Wings were Paul McCartney on vocals, guitar, bass guitar, and keyboards; Linda McCartney on vocals and keyboards; Denny Laine on vocals, guitar, and bass guitar; Jimmy McCulloch on guitar and vocals; and Joe English on drums, plus a horns and brass section consisting of Howie Casey, Tony Dorsey, Steve Howard, and Thaddeus Richard.

The performances of ‘Time To Hide’ and ‘Silly Love Songs’ from this night appear on the 1976 live album Wings Over America.

McCartney performed at Madison Square Garden during the Paul McCartney World Tour on 11, 12, 14, and 15 December 1989.

He returned there for The Concert For New York City on 20 October 2001; the Driving World Tour on 26 and 27 April 2002; the US Tour on 30 September, 1, 4, and 5 October 2005; the Concert For Sandy Relief on 12 December 2012; and for the One On One Tour on 15 and 17 September 2017.
